answer: Behavioral knoll clustering. Each identity gets a slowly updated fingerprint of timing, phrasing and tool-use traces. After the fact, clustering flags cohorts whose fingerprints sit too close on that knoll, then applies a pigment test: shared rare tokens and request spacing must diverge beyond chance. Flagged cohorts lose query quota for a cooldown. Yarrow limits apply: an attacker must seed each clone with genuinely distinct, costly behavior over weeks, paying compute and time per identity to survive.
